chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Hanifah al-Sabiq, who said:

Al-Mufaddal passed by us while I and my father-in-law were disputing over an inheritance. He stopped with us for a moment, then said, 'Come to the house.' We went to him, and he reconciled us between us for four hundred dirhams, which he paid to us from his own pocket, until each of us was assured by the other. Then he said, 'Indeed, it is not from my wealth, but Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered me: when two men from our companions dispute over something, I should reconcile between them and redeem them from his wealth.' So this was from the wealth of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: How did the companions use the Imam's wealth to settle disputes among themselves?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the practical application of *Sulh* (reconciliation) by Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who acted as an intermediary to resolve an inheritance dispute between Muhammad ibn Sinan and his father-in-law. Although he initially paid from his own pocket, he clarified that the funds were actually from Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) wealth, demonstrating the Imam’s active role in maintaining social harmony among his companions through financial intercession. This incident underscores the scholarly tradition of using communal or imamic resources to preserve kinship ties and prevent prolonged litigation.
